core_obligations: Part (1) (proof lines 3807-3817): since the second pair of maps is again a splitting, the composite of the second projection with the second splitting vanishes; substituting the displayed expressions for both and expanding gives g^n + h^n = 0, hence the two correction morphisms differ by a sign.

Part (2) (proof lines 3818-3822): expanding the expression for the second connecting morphism gives the first one plus two correction terms; using the relation between the two correction morphisms and the sign in the shifted differential identifies the difference as a homotopy boundary, which is the displayed formula.
proof_roadmap: Use that the second pair of maps is a splitting to get the vanishing composite.
Expand the composite to obtain the relation between the two correction morphisms.
Expand the second connecting morphism and rewrite the difference as a homotopy boundary.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a termwise split sequence of complexes of complexes, two choices of splitting differ by morphisms whose sign relation makes the difference of the two connecting morphisms a homotopy boundary, with the formula displayed explicitly (statement lines 3786-3804). The proof is a complete argument: the vanishing of the composite of the second projection with the second splitting is expanded to give the relation between the two correction morphisms (proof lines 3807-3817), and the expansion of the second connecting morphism, together with the sign in the shifted differential, identifies the difference as a boundary (proof lines 3818-3822). The non-formal content is the two displayed expansions. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
